s1.syndrome_frame: Multisystem disorder with chronic skin lesions and endocrine abnormalities
salient_findings: Numerous asymptomatic reddish-brownish papules, nodules, and plaques over the whole body
Central diabetes insipidus, growth retardation, and hypothyroidism
key_facts: 7-year medical history of skin lesions
Skin lesions began on bilateral eyelid margins and extended to trunk and extremities
Patient has central diabetes insipidus
Patient has growth retardation
Patient has hypothyroidism
Skin biopsy showed dense granulomatous infiltrate in the upper dermis
Immunohistochemical results were negative for CD1a and S-100, positive for CD68

Skin lesions are present on periocular areas, perioral areas, neck, shoulder, axillary folds, cubital fossa, wrists, palms, umbilical region, lateral abdomen, inguinal area, anogenital area, popliteal fossa, and ankles

shortlist.label: Erdheim-Chester disease
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the clinical presentation of chronic skin lesions, central diabetes insipidus, and growth retardation

shortlist.label: Xanthoma disseminatum
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with the skin biopsy findings of dense granulomatous infiltrate and the presence of skin lesions on multiple body areas

shortlist.label: Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Could explain the multisystem involvement, including skin lesions and endocrine abnormalities, although immunohistochemical results were negative for CD1a and S-100

shortlist.label: Multicentric reticulohistiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Possible diagnosis given the presence of skin lesions and potential systemic involvement, although less likely than Erdheim-Chester disease

shortlist.label: Non-Langerhans cell histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Considered due to the histiocytic nature of the skin lesions and the negative immunohistochemical results for CD1a and S-100

raw.rationale: The patient's 7-year medical history of skin lesions, central diabetes insipidus, growth retardation, and hypothyroidism, along with the skin biopsy findings of a dense granulomatous infiltrate and immunohistochemical results negative for CD1a and S-100 but positive for CD68, are consistent with Erdheim-Chester disease, a rare form of non-Langerhans cell histiocytosis.

rejected.label: Xanthoma disseminatum
rejected.why: Lack of specific mention of lipid-laden histiocytes in the biopsy findings

rejected.label: Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis
rejected.why: Immunohistochemical results were negative for CD1a and S-100, which are typically positive in Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis

rejected.label: Multicentric reticulohistiocytosis
rejected.why: No mention of characteristic mucocutaneous lesions or erosive arthritis

rejected.label: Non-Langerhans cell histiocytosis
rejected.why: Erdheim-Chester disease is a more specific diagnosis that fits the patient's presentation
